In the exact ASM, frequencies outside the propagating disk decay exponentially because cis imaginary. In Fresnel, after the quadratic approximation, all spatial frequencies behave as if they propagate. In the Fresnel approximation evanescent components do not exist and this can lead to nonphysical high-frequency behaviour. That is one reason Fresnel is very good for reasonably directional beams and longer propagation, but not for near-boundary, highly nonparaxial, or subwavelength-detail problems.

following_paragraphs: Remember that diffraction is nothing more than the changing interference among these plane-wave components as their relative phases evolve with z. Thus, we can say that the phase error is the relative transfer functions error, HASM/HF. Here we can already mention that if ΔH is same in (fx, fy) i.e. a common phase error, then intensity is not altered. But if ΔH is (fx, fy) dependent, then it will affect the interference i.e. the diffraction intensity.
